newsitem.title: USA: US senator to recommend new yield burning solution.
newsitem.headline: US senator to recommend new yield burning solution.

text.p: An influential U.S. Senator will recommend to the Justice Department and Internal Revenue Service this week that they invoke a 1986 federal law to recover millions of dollars the agencies allegedly are owed by Wall Street due to "yield burning," a source close to the issue said Wednesday.

The $1.3 trillion dollar municipal bond market has been rocked by recent charges that bond underwriters overbill issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond financing transactions, a practice known as yield burning.

Sen. Charles Grassley, a key member of the Senate Finance and Judiciary Committees, is expected to send letters to Justice and the Internal Revenue Service on Friday urging them to tap provisions of the 1986 False Claims Act to resolve yield burning, the source said.

That law permits the federal govenment to take action against any party that causes financial loss to the Treasury, the source said. The Treasury can get treble damages plus penalties, the source added.

The strategy would take the weight off municipal bond issuers who are being asked by Treasury to pay off yield-burning debts, even though most had no knowledge that their dealers may have engaged in the practice.

IRS notified issuers last year that they can avoid having interest on their bonds declared taxable by IRS if they pay Treasury the difference between the price they paid and the spot price of the securities on the purchase date, plus interest. Issuers are opposed to the plan.
